title: Steak au Poivre
subtitle: Pepper-crusted sirloin steaks with a cream pan sauce
excerpt: Steak au poivre is a French bistro dish where sirloin steaks are pressed into cracked black pepper to form a crust, then pan-fried and finished with a simple cream sauce built from the same pan. The whole thing takes under 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Steak au poivre became popular in French restaurants in the early twentieth century as a way of applying the preserving and flavour-boosting power of pepper to quality beef. It remains a French brasserie fixture.

content.text: Crack the black pepper coarsely using a pestle and mortar or the back of a heavy frying pan. You want rough, uneven pieces, not fine powder. Press them firmly into both sides of each steak so they stick during cooking.
Crack 2 to 3 tablespoons of black peppercorns coarsely using a pestle and mortar or the bottom of a heavy pan.
Season the steaks with salt on both sides, then press the cracked pepper firmly into both sides.

Heat half the butter in a large frying pan over a high heat until foaming. Add the steaks and cook for 3 minutes per side for medium-rare (adjust to your preference). Cook in batches if needed. Remove to a warm plate and rest for 5 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining butter to the pan. Add the Worcestershire sauce and stir, scraping up the pepper and meat juices.
Pour in the cream and add the Dijon mustard. Simmer, stirring, for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Pour the sauce over the rested steaks and serve immediately with fries or sauteed potatoes.

items.symptom: Pepper crust fell off during cooking.
items.cause: Pepper was not pressed in firmly enough before cooking.
items.fix: Press pepper hard into the steak and let it rest 5 minutes.

items.cause: Cream was not reduced long enough in the pan.
items.fix: Simmer cream for 3 to 4 minutes until it coats a spoon.
